temp._note: The primary temperature. none (the starting value) means no feed yet: one warning, no alarm, and the over-temperature cutoff cannot act, so your standalone heater thermostat is the only temperature protection. Set a real source before you turn outputs on: driver ds18b20_sysfs (a DS18B20 on a Pi or any Linux board), jsonl (newest line of a file, {"ts": ..., "temp_c": ...}) or http_json (a URL that answers with JSON). See docs/QUICKSTART.md, 'Temperature and light sources'.
temp.label: Tank thermometer

probe_temp._note: Optional second opinion (a probe on a Pi, for example); delete this input if you have none. Logged beside the Inkbird and compared by the setpoint watch; never an alarm of its own.
probe_temp.label: Pi probe

lifeguard._note: The independent watchdog (scripts/lifeguard.py, compose service lifeguard). It always observes and alerts: water beyond the hard band (alarm_c widened by hard_margin_c), no thermometer for blind_min, the controller silent for controller_silent_min, low disk. safe_mode.enabled lets it also latch safe mode on over-temperature or a silent controller: every light off, heater left to its own thermostat, until the cause has been clear for release_after_min (latch auto) or `lifeguard.py reset --yes` (latch manual). Off by default, like every output.

redundancy._note: Several thermometers, one decision (scripts/tank_vote.py). failover true: when the primary temperature cannot be used, the over-temperature cutoff, the heater gate and the alarm band act on a healthy backup (probe_temp) instead of going blind. Off: the backup is only reported.

itc_setpoints._note: Cue-driven Inkbird T1/T2 (tank_itc.py). Off. On, the tick writes data/itc/target.json from the plan's temperature cue (T1 = target - below_f, T2 = target + above_f, in F) and scripts/itc_setpoints.py applies it through the Android app. It targets the sandbox app unless ITC_PKG says otherwise; the real app is refused.

cooling._note: Over-temperature cutoff + fan stub (tank_cool.py). Acts only when outputs.enabled AND cooling.enabled are true. Cuts the listed plugs at setpoint + cutoff_above_c (never above limits.alarm_c[1]); fans are wanted at setpoint + cutoff_above_c / 2, and by fans.on_by_c (83.5 F) at the latest (stub: records only). The ladder above the 83 F cap: heat cut-off 83 F (heater.cut_off_c), fans 83.5 F, plugs cut and alarm 84 F (limits.alarm_c[1]). Until the calendar starts (2026-11-01) 'plan' has no set point and only the alarm ceiling applies; use a number for a fixed set point.

verify._note: Cue -> action -> verify (tank_verify.py). After a command reads back, the effect is checked on later ticks: the plug's watts when it reports them, and the lux sensor for any channel with min_lux_change set (lux the lamp should add or remove at the sensor; leave null for a lamp the sensor cannot see). A command whose effect never shows raises effect_failed:<plug>.
